newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mir commander says dark times over.
newsitem.headline: Mir commander says dark times over.

text.p: The commander of Russia's crippled Mir space station said on Monday that trying times on board had taught important lessons to him and his crew, now preparing to hand over to a relief team.

"We have gone through some very dark times but we are over them. Now we are focusing on getting the station ready for the new crew to make repairs," commander Vasily Tsibliyev said in a live interview between the station and Johannesburg.
"We have learnt valuable lessons for the future."
The trouble began on June 25 when Mir's Spektr module was holed in a collision with a cargo in the station's worst accident in 11 years in orbit.

Things got worse when one of the three men on board, trying to repair damage to a solar panel, crashed the computer, sending Mir tumbling through space with its electricity supply, already on half-power, down to the minimum.
The South African link-up with Mir was organised by Britain's De Montfort University as part of a human development and distance learning conference.
Tsibliyev, 43, did not comment on his health following reports that he developed stress-related heart trouble after the series of problems plaguing the space mission.
U.S. space agency physicist Michael Foale, who has been on Mir since flying up in a previous shuttle flight in May, said the crew flew over South Africa several times a day.
"We are enjoying South Africa from space," he said.
Tsibliyev and flight engineer Alexander Lazutkin will keep Mir ticking over in orbit until they hand over to replacements in about two weeks.
